rows.label: Chart data: revenue and EBITDA — paragraph 1

limitations: Produced in a host session and accepted by the CP-OS check.
Literal checked analytical handoff, not native contract acceptance; source qualifications and gaps remain.

- EBITDA (Reported) is derived, not stated: the issuer prints no unadjusted EBITDA, so every reported-basis ratio rests on operating income plus depreciation and amortization, which includes the 2024 gain on facility sales and the 2026 contract-termination revenue; this restricts the leverage and interest cover charts for fiscal 2024 and the 2026 periods. The action that would close it is the issuer stating an unadjusted EBITDA; until then both bases stay labelled and the adjusted ratios are the better reading. Severity High. - Revenue from contract termination is not supplied for fiscal 2025 and fiscal 2024, because the annual report has no such line, and for the nine-month and quarter 2025 comparatives, because the quarterly report prints a dash; no zero is stated. This restricts year-on-year comparison of that line only, and no action is needed because the agreement began in 2026. Severity Low. - Several other lines are not supplied for single columns: the loss from early extinguishment of debt and debt issuance costs where the source prints a dash, the managed care payer advance lines in some periods, liabilities held for sale and income tax payable at year-end 2025 where the source prints a dash, liabilities held for sale at 2026-09-30 where the line is not presented, and net gains from the sale of investments in the interim cash flows where the line is not presented. Each is shown as not supplied, never as zero, and none changes a fixed row or a checked identity. Severity Low. - Discrete third-quarter cash flows are not supplied because the cash flow statement is year to date; the third-quarter columns exist only in the income statement. This restricts quarterly cash analysis, and the nine-month columns are the finest cash flow period available. Severity Low. - Revolver availability at 2024-12-31 is not supplied: the 2025 annual report states availability only at 2025-12-31, after the new facility replaced the old one. This leaves undrawn committed facilities and cash plus revolver unsupplied for fiscal 2024 and restricts the liquidity trend; the 2024 annual report would close it. Severity Low. - No subsidiary guarantee of the unsecured notes is described, although the annual report calls those notes effectively subordinated to the obligations of subsidiaries, and the legal rank of the revolver against the notes, and of finance leases, mortgages and other notes, is not stated as a single rank, so those instruments are left out of the debt stack. This restricts the debt stack to the ten series of senior notes and the priority reading to the notes only; the indentures and credit agreement would close it. Severity Medium. - Carrying values by instrument are not disclosed, so each instrument keeps its disclosed principal and one financing cost adjustment row of minus 98 carries issue costs and discounts. This restricts any instrument-level carrying-value analysis; no action is needed for the aggregate, which reconciles exactly. Severity Low. - The day of maturity is not stated for the 2028 secured notes, the 2028 unsecured notes or the 2034 unsecured notes, and neither month nor day is stated for the 2029, both 2030 and 2031 secured notes or the 2031 unsecured notes; the maturity of finance leases, mortgages and other notes is not itemised. The June 2028 date for the 2028 secured notes is the earliest maturity the quarterly report states, so it is inferred. The maturity ladder is by calendar year and is unaffected, but a day-level wall cannot be drawn. Severity Low. - The issuer states a net debt to Adjusted EBITDA ratio in each earnings release without defining net debt. Recomputed with carrying-value debt less cash over last-twelve-months issuer Adjusted EBITDA, the ratio equals the issuer figures at 2025-12-31 and 2026-09-30, so Source readiness was wrong to say the ratio could not be reproduced for those two dates; the ratios stated for 2026-03-31 and 2026-06-30 were not tested because no figure was extracted from the first and second quarter reports. The definition remains inferred from a match rather than stated. Severity Low. - The executed indentures, the credit agreement and the letter of credit facility agreement are not supplied, and the filings state covenant levels only in words and no covenant ratio value for the issuer. Covenant headroom is therefore not calculable and no conclusion on it is drawn; the action that would close it is supplying those documents. Severity Medium. - No document is dated after 2026-10-29 and no event after 2026-09-30 with a stated effect on net debt appears in the sources read, so the post-balance-sheet table states none; the seven days to the as-of date are not covered, and later filings could change the position. Severity Low. - Operating lease liabilities are not itemised in the statements read, so they are outside total debt and outside this module's leverage; the terms and timing of the redemption rights behind redeemable noncontrolling interests are also not supplied. Both restrict a broader adjusted-debt reading, and the annual report lease and noncontrolling interest notes are the place to close them. Severity Low.

facts.label: Transaction summary and new debt issues
facts.text: The CommonSpirit Health arrangements are the defining transaction of 2026. On 2026-01-27 Tenet and CommonSpirit agreed to conclude the Conifer services contract, which had been scheduled to run to the end of 2032, by the end of 2026, and the transition of services is now expected to be substantially complete by 2026-10-30; CommonSpirit agreed to pay USD 1,900 million in annual installments over three years, of which USD 540 million was satisfied on the day by offsetting the USD 540 million Conifer owed for redeeming CommonSpirit's 23.8% minority interest in Conifer, effective 2026-01-01. The rest is a non-interest-bearing note of USD 1,360 million, with annual payments of about USD 453 million due in January 2027, January 2028 and January 2029, carried at USD 1,262 million of present value at 2026-09-30, USD 98 million below face value. facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Revenue durability is exposed to payer policy rather than to demand. Same-hospital adjusted admissions rose 2.1% in the nine months, but Medicaid rose to 11.90% of hospital patient revenue from 11.19% and exchange-covered admissions fell after enhanced premium credits expired, in a footprint where over half of licensed beds are in four states that have not expanded Medicaid. The One Big Beautiful Bill Act, whose most consequential provisions start in 2027, and Medicaid disproportionate share reductions scheduled from 2027-10-01 may cut Medicaid and supplemental payments, which the filings do not size, and the top ten managed care payers produced 69% of managed care revenue. facts.label: Business profile and credit linkage
facts.text: Tenet is a scaled, diversified operator whose cash flows are anchored in hospitals but are increasingly earned in outpatient surgery. facts.label: Business profile and credit linkage
facts.text: The portfolio has been reshaped by disposals and financing events that matter for credit. In 2024 Tenet sold fourteen hospitals and six surgery centers, with USD 4,981 million of proceeds from sales of facilities and other assets, in the year it redeemed USD 2,100 million of secured notes and repurchased USD 672 million of shares; in 2025 it acquired controlling interests in 27 surgery centers and one surgical hospital; and in 2026 it ended the CommonSpirit services contract and refinanced the 2027 secured notes into 2034 unsecured notes. These steps lowered the near-term maturity wall and moved the business toward outpatient care, which the issuer says has generated significantly higher margins than inpatient services, at the cost of a revenue cycle contract that ends and a stack in which 62.21% of principal is still secured. facts.label: Ownership, group structure and financial policy
facts.text: Ownership is public and no controlling holder or sponsor is named, which removes the usual dividend recapitalization and fee extraction channels, but control is not confirmed because board composition and beneficial ownership sit in a proxy statement that was not supplied. The structure matters more for ranking than for ownership: the secured notes are guaranteed by wholly owned domestic hospital subsidiaries and secured by a pledge of their capital stock, the unsecured notes carry no described subsidiary guarantee and are effectively subordinated to the secured notes and to subsidiary obligations, and 62.21% of principal is secured notes, so unsecured creditors rely on residual value after secured claims and minority partners. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_thc-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 145–146; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C07

facts.label: Revenue drivers and pricing power
facts.text: Hospital growth is volume-led, with pricing held back by payer mix in the third quarter. Same-hospital admissions rose 2.8% in the third quarter and 1.8% in the nine months, adjusted admissions rose 3.2% and 2.1%, but net patient service revenue per adjusted admission rose only 0.2% in the third quarter because strength in commercial employer revenue was offset by unfavorable payer mix from fewer exchange admissions. Pricing power is therefore constrained where the mix shifts toward Medicaid and uninsured patients, and revenue stays predictable only while coverage holds. facts.label: Cost structure and margin resilience
facts.text: Labor is the dominant cost and the main source of operating leverage. Salaries, wages and benefits were 39.6% of nine-month net operating revenues, supplies and other operating expenses make up most of the rest, and the 1.5 percentage point fall in the labor share is worth about USD 249.41 million at nine-month revenue, so each point of labor share moves nine-month Adjusted EBITDA by 4.35%. Margins can be defended under moderate volume pressure through staffing and supply chain management, but a payer-mix shock lowers revenue per admission while staffing is largely fixed, which is how the margin gain would reverse. facts.label: Policy, macro and technology factors
facts.text: Political and regulatory factors are a primary credit driver. The One Big Beautiful Bill Act adds Medicaid work requirements, caps on state-directed payments and limits on provider taxes from 2027, Medicaid disproportionate share reductions are scheduled from 2027-10-01, and enhanced premium credits for marketplace plans expired at the end of 2025; four of the eight states in which Tenet operates hospitals have expanded Medicaid, and over half of licensed beds are in four states that have not. The mechanism is fewer insured patients and lower or delayed supplemental payments, which reduces hospital revenue per admission and, because supplemental payments are part of the revolver borrowing base, could also reduce borrowing availability. facts.label: Downside scenario
facts.text: The downside scenario starts in 2027, when the first provisions of the One Big Beautiful Bill Act take effect and Medicaid disproportionate share reductions are scheduled from 2027-10-01, on top of the loss of exchange-covered admissions already visible in 2026. The first operational break is a further shift of hospital payer mix toward Medicaid and uninsured patients, where Medicaid already rose to 11.90% of patient revenue, with lower or delayed supplemental payments. That cuts revenue per admission while staffing cost stays largely fixed, so hospital Adjusted EBITDA of USD 2,258 million for the nine months falls faster than revenue, and the loss of earnings from the ended services contract adds to the base effect. facts.text: The financial transmission is anchored on Tenet's own earlier earnings: if last-twelve-month Adjusted EBITDA of USD 5,004 million returned to the 2025 level of USD 4,566 million, net leverage would be 2.31x, at the 2024 level of USD 3,995 million it would be 2.65x with interest cover of 4.81x, and free cash flow excluding the offset would fall to about USD 2,350 million against returns of USD 2,651 million, a shortfall of about USD 301 million a year if returns continued. Cash of USD 2,674 million would cover that shortfall for about 8.88 years, and management can cut repurchases, which have no minimum, so liquidity distress is not the likely outcome; the consequence is rising net debt and weaker leverage, and refinancing the USD 1,931 million due in 2028, which includes USD 600 million of secured notes due June 2028 and USD 1,250 million of unsecured notes due October 2028, in a weaker market than the one in which the 2034 notes were sold at a 6.25% coupon. facts.label: Overall credit view
facts.text: Overall, Tenet presents an adequate business profile supported by scale, an ambulatory earnings base and committed liquidity, but credit quality is constrained by hospital payer-policy exposure and by returns that absorb 95.09% of free cash flow. Cash-flow durability appears adequate because interest cover is 6.03x and free cash flow converts about 55% of Adjusted EBITDA, but it depends on earnings holding near the current level. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on stable earnings through the 2028 maturities of USD 1,931 million and on market conditions, because debt has been refinanced and not repaid. The primary downside path is a Medicaid and exchange-driven payer-mix shift in 2027 that lowers hospital earnings while shareholder returns continue. Compared with other leveraged hospital issuers the profile cannot be placed, because no peer data were supplied. Further analysis would require covenant ratio levels and executed documents, the size of Medicaid supplemental payments, the earnings of the ended services contract and the proxy statement. The top risk is payer-policy pressure on hospital earnings. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); Source readiness (CP-0); calculation C43; 10-Q_2026-09-30_thc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 52

limitations: Produced in a host session and accepted by the CP-OS check.
Literal checked analytical handoff, not native contract acceptance; source qualifications and gaps remain.

- Covenant ratio levels and the executed credit agreement, indentures and letter of credit agreement are not supplied, so covenant headroom is not calculable and the liquidity and sponsor conclusions rest on the issuer's summaries; one risk factor says debt covenants restrict dividends while the covenant note says the secured notes' indentures place no restriction on dividends or repurchases, and the conflict is left unresolved. The executed documents would close it. Severity Medium. - Medicaid supplemental payments are not sized beyond the USD 32 million prior-year benefit in the third quarter, so the effect of the 2027 policy changes on hospital earnings is described by mechanism and not by amount. Federal and state implementation guidance, and the issuer's own estimate if it gives one, would close it. Severity Medium. - The earnings contributed by the CommonSpirit services contract before it ends are not stated, so the 2027 earnings base cannot be estimated beyond the 2026 outlook. A segment disclosure on that business would close it. Severity Medium. - The terms and timing of partner put rights behind USD 2,179 million of redeemable minority interests are not stated, so the claim on group cash cannot be sized. The partnership agreements would close it. Severity Low. - No net leverage target, payout policy or capital allocation framework is stated in the documents read, so leverage tolerance is inferred from behavior. Management presentations would close it. Severity Low. - No peer, rating or market-implied reference is supplied, so the profile is not ranked against similar issuers. A peer set and dated market data would close it. Severity Low. - No document is dated after 2026-10-29, so events between that date and the as-of date are not covered. Later filings would close it. Severity Low.

Source readiness for TENET HEALTHCARE CORP (Tenet Healthcare Corporation, ticker THC) as of 2026-11-05 under the credit snapshot pathway. The scope is the seven supplied issuer documents, one annual report for fiscal 2025, three quarterly reports for 2026 and three 2026 earnings releases, tested against the evidence needs of Financial foundation, Business & governance and Fundamental credit.

No external sources were used.
## Findings
### Bottom line

The supplied filings and earnings releases support a credit snapshot of TENET HEALTHCARE CORP as of 2026-11-05, so creditors can rest leverage, liquidity and maturity conclusions on primary issuer disclosures, but not on executed financing terms, ratings or note-level market prices.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_thc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 118; 10-Q_2026-09-30_thc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 2–3; EX-99.1_2026-10-29_thc-20260930ex991earningsr.htm.jsonl, page 1

Financial foundation, Business & governance and Fundamental credit are each ready with limitations. The main limits are the missing proxy statement for governance detail, the absence of the indentures and credit agreement behind the covenant summaries, and no document dated after 2026-10-29. No credit conclusion is drawn in this module.
### Key findings

The set holds one audited annual report for 2025, three unaudited quarterly reports for 2026 and an earnings release for each 2026 quarter, so the latest quarter, the nine-month comparatives and a last-twelve-months window to the third quarter of 2026 can all be read from supplied statements. The latest document is dated 2026-10-29, one week before the as-of date, so events in that week are not covered.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_thc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 184; 10-Q_2026-09-30_thc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 2–3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_thc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 54; calculation C3

The notes to the 2025 annual report and the latest quarterly report print each note series, the revolving credit facility, the letter of credit facility and the covenant descriptions, together with the September 2026 refinancing and the issuer's statement that it complied with its covenants. The indentures, the credit agreement and any guarantor financial split are not supplied, so covenant levels and guarantor terms rest on the issuer's own summaries and headroom cannot be tested from the documents.

The three earnings releases state a net debt to Adjusted EBITDA ratio without defining net debt, so that ratio cannot be reproduced from the sources. The third quarter of 2026 also carries contract-termination revenue and transition benefits from the CommonSpirit agreement: the termination revenue is reported on its own line and falls outside Adjusted EBITDA, while a catch-up adjustment and a transition benefit sit inside it, so reported and adjusted earnings have to be read together.
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest case against readiness is the absence of the executed financing documents: if a credit view turns on covenant headroom, guarantor priority or collateral value, the issuer's summaries would not be enough and those questions would stay conditional on further documents. A published credit rating, note-level market prices or a filing dated after 2026-10-29 would also change the picture.

## Findings
### Bottom line

Net leverage on issuer-adjusted EBITDA improved to 2.11x at 2026-09-30 from 2.25x at 2025-12-31, so the cushion against debt service widened, but net leverage of 1.68x on reported EBITDA is flattered by CommonSpirit termination revenue and is not a safe anchor.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_thc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 2–3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_thc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 12–13; 10-Q_2026-09-30_thc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 24–25; 10-K_2025-12-31_thc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 174; calculation C03; calculation C11

The September 2026 refinancing replaced the 2027 secured notes and part of the 2028 unsecured notes with 2034 notes, so the nearest large maturity is now 2028, and USD 2,674 million of cash plus an undrawn USD 1,900 million revolver stand ahead of it. Interest cover on adjusted EBITDA reached 6.03x over the last twelve months, but repurchases and distributions to noncontrolling interests absorbed USD 2,651 million of USD 3,328 million of free cash flow.

### Financial interpretation

Net debt on carrying values moved from USD 10,154 million at 2024-12-31 to USD 10,288 million at 2025-12-31 and USD 10,569 million at 2026-09-30, while gross debt stayed between USD 13,171 million and USD 13,243 million and cash fell from USD 3,019 million to USD 2,674 million. Net leverage on issuer-adjusted EBITDA therefore improved from 2.54x to 2.25x to 2.11x because adjusted EBITDA grew to USD 5,004 million over the last twelve months, not because debt was repaid, so the gain holds only while that earnings level holds.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_thc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 118; 10-Q_2026-09-30_thc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_thc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 24–25; calculation C03; calculation C11; calculation C36

On reported EBITDA derived from operating income and depreciation and amortization, net leverage was 1.50x, 2.35x and 1.68x, but those denominators carry a USD 2,916 million gain on facility sales in 2024 and USD 1,472 million of CommonSpirit contract-termination revenue in the first nine months of 2026. That revenue is recognised against a USD 1,360 million note receivable, payable in three annual installments of about USD 453 million from January 2027, and a USD 540 million offset, so it reaches reported earnings before it reaches cash and reported leverage is not a safe primary reading for 2026.

Cash interest paid was USD 830 million over the last twelve months against USD 865 million in 2025, and adjusted EBITDA covered it 6.03x against 5.28x in 2025 and 4.69x in 2024. The September 2026 refinancing replaced secured and unsecured notes with 2034 unsecured notes at a higher coupon than the notes it retired, so cover should not improve because of the refinancing itself, and accrued interest expense of USD 612 million for the nine months exceeds cash paid of USD 464 million by a coupon-timing difference of USD 148 million.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_thc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 121; 10-Q_2026-09-30_thc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 2–4; 10-Q_2026-09-30_thc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 12–13; calculation C13; calculation C39

Operating cash flow of USD 3,507 million for the nine months includes USD 540 million of CommonSpirit consideration settled by offset, which the quarterly report also counts in the financing outflow for the redemption of CommonSpirit's interest in Conifer, so free cash flow over the last twelve months is USD 3,328 million with the offset and USD 2,788 million without it. Repurchases of USD 1,813 million and distributions to noncontrolling interests of USD 838 million together absorbed USD 2,651 million, about 95% of the free cash flow without the offset, which leaves little internal cash to reduce debt.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_thc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 49–50; 10-Q_2026-09-30_thc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 3–4; EX-99.1_2026-10-29_thc-20260930ex991earningsr.htm.jsonl, page 14; calculation C21; calculation C22; calculation C25; calculation C26

The 2028 maturities include USD 1,250 million of unsecured notes due October 2028 and USD 600 million of secured notes due June 2028, and the revolver's fixed charge coverage test applies only if excess availability falls below USD 150 million, so near-term refinancing risk is low and the 2028 maturities are the next concentration.

The agreement of 2026-01-27 with CommonSpirit and the September 2026 refinancing both precede the 2026-09-30 balance sheet and are inside it, and no later event with a stated effect on net debt appears in the sources read; the first installment of the CommonSpirit note, about USD 453 million, is due in January 2027. ## Gaps

- EBITDA (Reported) is derived, not stated: the issuer prints no unadjusted EBITDA, so every reported-basis ratio rests on operating income plus depreciation and amortization, which includes the 2024 gain on facility sales and the 2026 contract-termination revenue; this restricts the leverage and interest cover charts for fiscal 2024 and the 2026 periods. The action that would close it is the issuer stating an unadjusted EBITDA; until then both bases stay labelled and the adjusted ratios are the better reading. Severity High.

- Revenue from contract termination is not supplied for fiscal 2025 and fiscal 2024, because the annual report has no such line, and for the nine-month and quarter 2025 comparatives, because the quarterly report prints a dash; no zero is stated. This restricts year-on-year comparison of that line only, and no action is needed because the agreement began in 2026. Severity Low.

- Several other lines are not supplied for single columns: the loss from early extinguishment of debt and debt issuance costs where the source prints a dash, the managed care payer advance lines in some periods, liabilities held for sale and income tax payable at year-end 2025 where the source prints a dash, liabilities held for sale at 2026-09-30 where the line is not presented, and net gains from the sale of investments in the interim cash flows where the line is not presented. Each is shown as not supplied, never as zero, and none changes a fixed row or a checked identity. Severity Low.

- Discrete third-quarter cash flows are not supplied because the cash flow statement is year to date; the third-quarter columns exist only in the income statement. This restricts quarterly cash analysis, and the nine-month columns are the finest cash flow period available. Severity Low.

- Revolver availability at 2024-12-31 is not supplied: the 2025 annual report states availability only at 2025-12-31, after the new facility replaced the old one. This leaves undrawn committed facilities and cash plus revolver unsupplied for fiscal 2024 and restricts the liquidity trend; the 2024 annual report would close it. Severity Low.

- No subsidiary guarantee of the unsecured notes is described, although the annual report calls those notes effectively subordinated to the obligations of subsidiaries, and the legal rank of the revolver against the notes, and of finance leases, mortgages and other notes, is not stated as a single rank, so those instruments are left out of the debt stack. This restricts the debt stack to the ten series of senior notes and the priority reading to the notes only; the indentures and credit agreement would close it. Severity Medium.

- Carrying values by instrument are not disclosed, so each instrument keeps its disclosed principal and one financing cost adjustment row of minus 98 carries issue costs and discounts. This restricts any instrument-level carrying-value analysis; no action is needed for the aggregate, which reconciles exactly. Severity Low.

- The day of maturity is not stated for the 2028 secured notes, the 2028 unsecured notes or the 2034 unsecured notes, and neither month nor day is stated for the 2029, both 2030 and 2031 secured notes or the 2031 unsecured notes; the maturity of finance leases, mortgages and other notes is not itemised. The June 2028 date for the 2028 secured notes is the earliest maturity the quarterly report states, so it is inferred. The maturity ladder is by calendar year and is unaffected, but a day-level wall cannot be drawn. Severity Low.

- The issuer states a net debt to Adjusted EBITDA ratio in each earnings release without defining net debt. Recomputed with carrying-value debt less cash over last-twelve-months issuer Adjusted EBITDA, the ratio equals the issuer figures at 2025-12-31 and 2026-09-30, so Source readiness was wrong to say the ratio could not be reproduced for those two dates; the ratios stated for 2026-03-31 and 2026-06-30 were not tested because no figure was extracted from the first and second quarter reports. The definition remains inferred from a match rather than stated. Severity Low.

- The executed indentures, the credit agreement and the letter of credit facility agreement are not supplied, and the filings state covenant levels only in words and no covenant ratio value for the issuer. Covenant headroom is therefore not calculable and no conclusion on it is drawn; the action that would close it is supplying those documents. Severity Medium.

- No document is dated after 2026-10-29 and no event after 2026-09-30 with a stated effect on net debt appears in the sources read, so the post-balance-sheet table states none; the seven days to the as-of date are not covered, and later filings could change the position. Severity Low.

- Operating lease liabilities are not itemised in the statements read, so they are outside total debt and outside this module's leverage; the terms and timing of the redemption rights behind redeemable noncontrolling interests are also not supplied. Both restrict a broader adjusted-debt reading, and the annual report lease and noncontrolling interest notes are the place to close them. Severity Low.

Business and governance fact base for TENET HEALTHCARE CORP (Tenet Healthcare Corporation) as of 2026-11-05 under the credit snapshot pathway. Scope is the issuer's business and operating model, ownership and control, governance and shareholder behaviour, transactions and new debt issues, and dated history, from the supplied annual report, three 2026 quarterly reports and earnings releases.
## Sources

No external sources were used.
## Findings
### Bottom line

Tenet is a listed hospital and surgery-center operator with no identified controlling holder, so creditor risk lies in payer mix and Medicaid policy, not ownership. The CommonSpirit agreement turns a recurring services contract into USD 1,900 million of installments.

Hospitals produce about three quarters of revenue, yet Ambulatory Care earns 40.91% of nine-month Adjusted EBITDA and 39.35% of that belongs to minority partners, so parent debt service relies on subsidiary cash. Repurchases of USD 1,615 million in the nine months are the main shareholder-return behaviour, the refinancings were creditor-neutral to supportive, and sponsor and governance risk is medium because governance detail is incomplete, not because adverse conduct was found.

Basis: EX-99.1_2026-10-29_thc-20260930ex991earningsr.htm.jsonl, page 3; EX-99.1_2026-10-29_thc-20260930ex991earningsr.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-K_2025-12-31_thc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 50; calculation C08; calculation C10
### Key findings

The business has two segments: acute care hospitals, physician practices and the revenue cycle business Conifer in Hospital Operations and Services, and a large network of surgery centers and surgical hospitals held through USPI in Ambulatory Care. At 2026-09-30 the hospital segment operated 51 hospitals in eight states, and about 74% of its outpatient centers were in Arizona and Texas at 2025-12-31, so regional payer, regulatory or weather events can hit a large share of cash flow at once.

Ownership is public, and no sponsor, fund or controlling holder is named in the supplied filings, but board composition, executive detail and beneficial ownership sit in a proxy statement that was not supplied, so control cannot be confirmed. Repurchases cut shares outstanding by 8.48% between 2026-01-30 and 2026-10-23 and USD 1,875 million of authorization remained at 2026-09-30, which shows a policy of returning cash that creditors should monitor against leverage.

On 2026-01-27 Tenet agreed with CommonSpirit Health to end the Conifer services contract early, to receive USD 1,900 million in annual installments over three years, of which USD 540 million was settled by offset against Conifer's redemption of CommonSpirit's minority interest, leaving a note of USD 1,360 million payable from January 2027. Tenet recognized USD 1,472 million of contract-termination revenue in the nine months while only the USD 540 million settled by offset has been received, so earnings run ahead of cash, and Tenet now owns all of Conifer. The issuer's Adjusted EBITDA excludes the contract-termination revenue but includes a USD 147 million net favorable transition impact in the third quarter.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_thc-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 175–176; 10-Q_2026-03-31_thc-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-06-30_thc-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_thc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_thc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-Q_2026-09-30_thc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 10; EX-99.1_2026-10-29_thc-20260930ex991earningsr.htm.jsonl, page 2; EX-99.1_2026-10-29_thc-20260930ex991earningsr.htm.jsonl, page 8; calculation C17

Managed care supplies most hospital patient revenue, and the Medicaid share rose to 11.90% in the nine months from 11.19% a year earlier while exchange admissions fell, so payer mix is moving against Tenet, and the top ten managed care payers produced 69% of managed care patient revenue in 2025, so contract renewals matter. The One Big Beautiful Bill Act, whose most consequential provisions take effect from 2027, may materially reduce Medicaid payments and supplemental payment programs, which is the main policy risk to hospital margins.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_thc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 17; 10-Q_2026-09-30_thc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 28; 10-Q_2026-09-30_thc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 35–36; 10-K_2025-12-31_thc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 17; 10-K_2025-12-31_thc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 30; calculation C12; calculation C13

The two refinancings of the last year, in November 2025 and September 2026, extended maturities and retired secured notes without new debt-funded distributions, and the disclosed behaviour is repurchases funded from operating cash flow with senior notes outstanding unchanged at USD 12,662 million. The issuer's own summary says the secured notes' indentures place no limit on restricted payments, so legal capacity to return more cash is wide even though willingness shown so far is moderate.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_thc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 145; 10-K_2025-12-31_thc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 148; 10-Q_2026-09-30_thc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-Q_2026-09-30_thc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 50; Source readiness (CP-0)
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest contrary evidence is that repurchases and distributions to noncontrolling interests absorbed 75.28% of nine-month free cash flow and 88.31% of adjusted free cash flow while the secured notes' indentures, as the issuer summarises them, restrict neither dividends nor repurchases. A debt-funded repurchase, a controlling holder or related-party payments shown in the proxy statement, or a payment restriction in the executed documents would move sponsor and governance risk to high or low, and a faster Medicaid supplemental payment cut would weaken the operating view.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_thc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 148; 10-K_2025-12-31_thc-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 177–178; 10-K_2025-12-31_thc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 17; EX-99.1_2026-10-29_thc-20260930ex991earningsr.htm.jsonl, page 14; calculation C26; calculation C25
### Limitations

The proxy statement was not supplied, so board composition, executive biographies, compensation, related-party transactions and beneficial ownership are not established; only board oversight of compliance and risk and the audit position can be stated.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_thc-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 177–178; 10-K_2025-12-31_thc-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 112–113; Source readiness (CP-0)
The indentures, the credit agreement and the CommonSpirit agreements are not supplied, so legal capacity, collateral and the exact payment terms rest on the issuer's summaries in its filings.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_thc-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 148–149; 10-Q_2026-09-30_thc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 5; Source readiness (CP-0)

USPI's ownership percentage in each facility, the exact terms of the partners' redemption rights and the revenue of Conifer by client are not stated, so noncontrolling cash leakage and Conifer client concentration cannot be sized; the annual report says only that some partnership agreements could oblige Tenet to buy the minority interests on specified events.

The CommonSpirit Health arrangements are the defining transaction of 2026. On 2026-01-27 Tenet and CommonSpirit agreed to conclude the Conifer services contract, which had been scheduled to run to the end of 2032, by the end of 2026, and the transition of services is now expected to be substantially complete by 2026-10-30; CommonSpirit agreed to pay USD 1,900 million in annual installments over three years, of which USD 540 million was satisfied on the day by offsetting the USD 540 million Conifer owed for redeeming CommonSpirit's 23.8% minority interest in Conifer, effective 2026-01-01. The rest is a non-interest-bearing note of USD 1,360 million, with annual payments of about USD 453 million due in January 2027, January 2028 and January 2029, carried at USD 1,262 million of present value at 2026-09-30, USD 98 million below face value.

In September 2026 Tenet issued USD 2,000 million of 6.250% senior unsecured notes due 2034 in a private placement, and used the proceeds with cash on hand to redeem all USD 1,500 million of the 5.125% senior secured first lien notes due 2027 and USD 500 million of the 6.125% senior notes due 2028. The quarterly report says this reduced secured debt and moved part of the near-term maturities to 2034, and a supplemental indenture dated 2026-09-22 is listed as an exhibit.

In November 2025 Tenet issued USD 1,500 million of 5.500% senior secured first lien notes due 2032 and USD 750 million of 6.000% senior unsecured notes due 2033, redeemed all USD 1,500 million of the 6.250% second lien notes due 2027 and USD 750 million of the 6.125% senior notes due 2028, and replaced its USD 1,500 million revolving credit facility with a new USD 1,900 million facility maturing 2030-11-04 while extending the letter of credit facility to the same date.

Other transactions are acquisitions, share repurchases and disposals. Tenet used USD 201 million of cash for acquisition-related activity in the nine months to 2026-09-30 against USD 266 million a year earlier, repurchased shares for USD 1,615 million in the nine months under a program whose authorization the board raised by USD 2,000 million in June 2026, and in 2024 sold fourteen hospitals in South Carolina, California and Alabama and six surgery centers for named gains totaling USD 2,878 million.

- The proxy statement is not supplied, so board composition, executive detail, compensation, beneficial ownership and related-party transactions are not established, which limits the ownership and governance registers; the 2026 proxy statement would close it. Severity Medium.

- The CommonSpirit agreements and the current report of 2026-02-02 are not supplied, so the note's security and acceleration terms are not stated and the split of the 250 difference between the USD 1,900 million consideration and the USD 1,650 million fiscal 2026 outlook revenue, which the release attributes to present value and amortization of an associated contract asset, is not sized; the agreements would close it. spans.text: ## Request

Fundamental credit synthesis for TENET HEALTHCARE CORP (Tenet Healthcare Corporation) as of 2026-11-05 under the credit snapshot pathway. Scope is business quality, ownership and financial policy, operating drivers, cash conversion, liquidity and refinancing capacity, the main downside path and its monitors, drawn from the supplied filings and the earlier Source readiness, Financial foundation and Business & governance analyses.
## Sources

No external sources were used.
## Findings
### Bottom line

Tenet's fundamental credit profile is adequate for a high-yield hospital operator and improving on earnings, but cash returns and Medicaid policy exposure keep deleveraging dependent on earnings growth, so creditors should expect stable rather than strengthening credit quality. Net debt to issuer-adjusted EBITDA fell to 2.11x at 2026-09-30 from 2.25x at 2025-12-31 because earnings rose while net debt grew by USD 281 million, and liquidity of USD 4,574 million is 2.16x the USD 2,115 million of debt due through 2028.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); EX-99.1_2026-10-29_thc-20260930ex991earningsr.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_thc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 12–13; calculation C01; calculation C02; calculation C04

The strongest support is liquidity ahead of the 2028 maturities and an ambulatory franchise that earns a 38.3% margin. The weakest dimension is free cash flow after returns: repurchases and distributions to partners took 95.09% of free cash flow excluding the CommonSpirit offset, and the primary downside path runs from lower Medicaid payments and fewer exchange-covered admissions in 2027 to hospital earnings.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); EX-99.1_2026-10-29_thc-20260930ex991earningsr.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_thc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 35–36; calculation C43
### Key findings

Earnings are larger and higher-margin than the hospital base alone suggests, but a large part of the ambulatory franchise belongs to partners. Ambulatory Care produced 24.53% of nine-month revenue and 40.91% of Adjusted EBITDA at a 38.3% margin against 18.0% for hospitals, and 39.35% of its Adjusted EBITDA is attributable to noncontrolling interests, so parent debt service relies on subsidiary cash that partners share. Net debt over Adjusted EBITDA after last-twelve-month distributions to partners is 2.54x, against the issuer's 2.11x.

Basis: EX-99.1_2026-10-29_thc-20260930ex991earningsr.htm.jsonl, page 3; EX-99.1_2026-10-29_thc-20260930ex991earningsr.htm.jsonl, page 13; Business & governance (CP-1A); Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C45; calculation C44; calculation C08

Leverage is moderate and has improved only through earnings. Net debt to issuer-adjusted EBITDA was 2.54x at 2024-12-31, 2.25x at 2025-12-31 and 2.11x at 2026-09-30 while net debt rose from USD 10,154 million to USD 10,569 million; excluding the USD 147 million net transition benefit in the third quarter the ratio is 2.18x, and at the 2025 earnings level it would be 2.31x. Adjusted EBITDA is 25.26% above its 2024 level, so the gain holds only while that level holds.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); EX-99.1_2026-10-29_thc-20260930ex991earningsr.htm.jsonl, page 2; calculation C09; calculation C10; calculation C14

Cash generation covers interest comfortably but is almost fully committed to shareholders and partners. Adjusted EBITDA covered cash interest 6.03x over the last twelve months and free cash flow excluding the offset was USD 2,788 million, 55.72% of Adjusted EBITDA, yet repurchases and distributions to partners absorbed USD 2,651 million, leaving USD 137 million. The repurchase program has no minimum and USD 1,875 million of authorization remains, so the return policy is a choice management can change.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_thc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 50; calculation C16; calculation C43; calculation C13

Liquidity leaves no refinancing pressure before 2028, but the debt stack is secured-heavy and costs more as low-coupon notes mature. Cash of USD 2,674 million and an undrawn USD 1,900 million revolver total USD 4,574 million against only USD 184 million due before 2028 and USD 2,115 million through 2028; 62.21% of principal is senior secured first lien notes, and refinancing the 2029 and 2030 notes that carry the lowest coupons at the 6.25% paid in September 2026 would add about USD 55.19 million of annual interest.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_thc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 12–13; 10-Q_2026-09-30_thc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 52; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C01; calculation C03; calculation C02; calculation C07; calculation C33

Revenue durability is exposed to payer policy rather than to demand. Same-hospital adjusted admissions rose 2.1% in the nine months, but Medicaid rose to 11.90% of hospital patient revenue from 11.19% and exchange-covered admissions fell after enhanced premium credits expired, in a footprint where over half of licensed beds are in four states that have not expanded Medicaid. The One Big Beautiful Bill Act, whose most consequential provisions start in 2027, and Medicaid disproportionate share reductions scheduled from 2027-10-01 may cut Medicaid and supplemental payments, which the filings do not size, and the top ten managed care payers produced 69% of managed care revenue.

Basis: EX-99.1_2026-10-29_thc-20260930ex991earningsr.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-09-30_thc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 17; 10-Q_2026-09-30_thc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 35–36; 10-K_2025-12-31_thc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-K_2025-12-31_thc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 30; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C23

Margins are resilient on labor discipline but remain exposed to wage and liability costs. The consolidated Adjusted EBITDA margin rose to 23.0% from 21.4% and salaries fell to 39.6% of revenue from 41.1%, a change worth USD 249.41 million at nine-month revenue, but the margin includes the third-quarter transition benefit and would be 22.23% without it, a rise of 0.83 percentage points. Malpractice expense rose 21.81% to USD 296 million and wage pressure continues, so part of the margin gain could reverse if labor shortages returned.

Basis: EX-99.1_2026-10-29_thc-20260930ex991earningsr.htm.jsonl, page 2; EX-99.1_2026-10-29_thc-20260930ex991earningsr.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-Q_2026-09-30_thc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-Q_2026-09-30_thc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 40; 10-K_2025-12-31_thc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 11; calculation C26; calculation C28; calculation C29; calculation C24

The CommonSpirit termination lifts reported earnings ahead of cash and removes a contract whose earnings are not disclosed. Tenet recognized USD 1,472 million of contract-termination revenue in the nine months against USD 540 million received by offset; the USD 1,360 million note, carried at USD 1,262 million, pays about USD 453 million a year from January 2027 to January 2029, and Adjusted EBITDA excludes the revenue but includes a USD 147 million net transition benefit. The earnings the services contract contributes before it ends on 2026-12-31 are not stated, so the 2027 earnings base is uncertain.

Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_thc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_thc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 17; EX-99.1_2026-10-29_thc-20260930ex991earningsr.htm.jsonl, page 2; EX-99.1_2026-10-29_thc-20260930ex991earningsr.htm.jsonl, page 8

Financial policy is the weakest-evidenced dimension rather than an adverse one. Repurchases of USD 1,615 million in the nine months took cumulative use under the program to USD 3,125 million of USD 5,000 million authorized and cut shares outstanding by 8.48%; no controlling holder is named, but the proxy statement was not supplied and the issuer's own summary says the secured notes' indentures place no limit on restricted payments, so shareholder returns are a monitoring item and not a finding of extraction.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_thc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 148; 10-Q_2026-09-30_thc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 53; calculation C41
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence for a better view is that last-twelve-month Adjusted EBITDA is above its 2024 level by 25.26%, net leverage is 2.11x with USD 4,574 million of liquidity, and the returns that absorb 95.09% of free cash flow are largely discretionary: the repurchase program can be suspended, which would release up to USD 1,813 million a year at the last-twelve-month pace, and the CommonSpirit note adds about USD 453 million a year from January 2027, equal to 24.99% of those repurchases. The strongest evidence for a worse view is policy: payer-mix pressure is already visible in 2026 and the larger Medicaid changes start in 2027, with no disclosed estimate of their size.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_thc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_thc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 50; 10-Q_2026-09-30_thc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 35–36; calculation C14; calculation C01; calculation C43; calculation C42

The view would improve if repurchases fell below free cash flow and net debt declined for consecutive quarters, or if filings showed the Medicaid exposure to be small against hospital Adjusted EBITDA of USD 2,258 million for the nine months. ### Limitations

- No peer or sector comparison data are supplied, so the judgement that the profile is adequate for a high-yield hospital operator rests on Tenet's own history and policy exposure, and a weaker or stronger peer set would change how the profile ranks without changing the earnings and leverage trend.
Basis: Source readiness (CP-0)

- No agency rating, rating outlook or individual note price is supplied, so the refinancing conclusion rests on the issuer's own fair value of debt, which was 97.3% of carrying value at 2026-09-30 against 100.9% at 2025-12-31, and on the September 2026 placement; wider spreads would make the 2028 refinancing dearer than the cost estimate shows.

- Medicaid supplemental payments and the CommonSpirit services contract are not sized in earnings, so the downside scenario shows the transmission by mechanism and anchors the numbers on Tenet's own earlier earnings levels instead of an estimate of the loss.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_thc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 17; EX-99.1_2026-10-29_thc-20260930ex991earningsr.htm.jsonl, page 4; Business & governance (CP-1A)

- The liquidity conclusion counts the full USD 1,900 million revolver as available because the issuer states that availability, but the borrowing base includes Medicaid supplemental payments whose size is not stated, so availability could be lower if those payments fall.

- Redeemable minority interests of USD 2,179 million, of which USD 2,134 million belong to Ambulatory Care, sit outside net debt and could oblige Tenet to buy partners' interests on specified events, so net leverage of 2.11x understates claims on group cash by an amount the filings do not state.

- The downside sensitivities assume the whole fall in Adjusted EBITDA reaches free cash flow before tax and working capital effects, which overstates the cash effect, and assume returns continue at the last-twelve-month pace, which management can change.

### Business profile and credit linkage

Tenet is a scaled, diversified operator whose cash flows are anchored in hospitals but are increasingly earned in outpatient surgery. It operated 51 hospitals in eight states at 2026-09-30, with about 74% of its hospital outpatient centers in Arizona and Texas at 2025-12-31, and USPI runs a network of surgery centers and surgical hospitals in 37 states; last-twelve-month net operating revenues were USD 22,154 million. Hospitals produced 75.47% of nine-month revenue and 59.09% of Adjusted EBITDA, so a payer or regulatory shock in a few states reaches a large share of cash flow at once, while the ambulatory network spreads procedure volume across many facilities and physician partners.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_thc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 26; 10-K_2025-12-31_thc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 6; 10-K_2025-12-31_thc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 7; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C46

Revenue is transactional and regulated, not contracted: managed care supplies 68.51% of hospital patient service revenue, Medicare 15.19% and Medicaid 11.90%, so cash-flow visibility depends on payer contract renewals and government rate-setting, not on long-dated customer contracts. That supports a steady cash profile in normal conditions, because acute care volumes grew in 2026, but it gives creditors little contractual protection when payer mix or rates change.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_thc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 17; EX-99.1_2026-10-29_thc-20260930ex991earningsr.htm.jsonl, page 4; Business & governance (CP-1A)

The portfolio has been reshaped by disposals and financing events that matter for credit. In 2024 Tenet sold fourteen hospitals and six surgery centers, with USD 4,981 million of proceeds from sales of facilities and other assets, in the year it redeemed USD 2,100 million of secured notes and repurchased USD 672 million of shares; in 2025 it acquired controlling interests in 27 surgery centers and one surgical hospital; and in 2026 it ended the CommonSpirit services contract and refinanced the 2027 secured notes into 2034 unsecured notes. These steps lowered the near-term maturity wall and moved the business toward outpatient care, which the issuer says has generated significantly higher margins than inpatient services, at the cost of a revenue cycle contract that ends and a stack in which 62.21% of principal is still secured.
### Ownership, group structure and financial policy

Ownership is public and no controlling holder or sponsor is named, which removes the usual dividend recapitalization and fee extraction channels, but control is not confirmed because board composition and beneficial ownership sit in a proxy statement that was not supplied. The structure matters more for ranking than for ownership: the secured notes are guaranteed by wholly owned domestic hospital subsidiaries and secured by a pledge of their capital stock, the unsecured notes carry no described subsidiary guarantee and are effectively subordinated to the secured notes and to subsidiary obligations, and 62.21% of principal is secured notes, so unsecured creditors rely on residual value after secured claims and minority partners.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_thc-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 145–146; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C07

Minority partners are a second layer of claims. They are attributable for 39.35% of ambulatory Adjusted EBITDA, received USD 838 million of distributions over the last twelve months, and hold redeemable interests of USD 2,134 million in Ambulatory Care that could require Tenet to use cash flow or borrow if put rights were exercised. The issuer lists the exercise of put rights by joint venture partners among the events that could materially affect its cash requirements.

Basis: EX-99.1_2026-10-29_thc-20260930ex991earningsr.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_thc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 20; 10-Q_2026-09-30_thc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 51; 10-K_2025-12-31_thc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 49; Business & governance (CP-1A); Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C44

Financial policy has favored shareholder returns over debt repayment. Repurchases took shares outstanding down by 8.48% in about nine months, no common dividend appears in the cash flow statements, acquisition spending was modest at USD 201 million in the nine months, and the senior notes outstanding were unchanged at USD 12,662 million after two refinancings. No net leverage target or payout policy is stated in the documents read, and the issuer notes that early call premiums make debt repayment a costly way to deleverage, so leverage tolerance is revealed by behavior: issuer net leverage between 2.11x and 2.33x over the last three reported dates, with returns sized to free cash flow.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_thc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 50; 10-Q_2026-09-30_thc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 23; 10-Q_2026-09-30_thc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 53
### Revenue drivers and pricing power

Hospital growth is volume-led, with pricing held back by payer mix in the third quarter. Same-hospital admissions rose 2.8% in the third quarter and 1.8% in the nine months, adjusted admissions rose 3.2% and 2.1%, but net patient service revenue per adjusted admission rose only 0.2% in the third quarter because strength in commercial employer revenue was offset by unfavorable payer mix from fewer exchange admissions. Pricing power is therefore constrained where the mix shifts toward Medicaid and uninsured patients, and revenue stays predictable only while coverage holds.
Basis: EX-99.1_2026-10-29_thc-20260930ex991earningsr.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-09-30_thc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 28; 10-Q_2026-09-30_thc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 35

Ambulatory growth is price and acuity-led. Same-facility system-wide revenue rose 5.1% in the nine months with revenue per case up 6.0% and surgical cases down 0.8%, and the third-quarter case decline was 1.5%, so growth depends on the pricing and mix of procedures, not on rising volumes, which leaves it exposed to payer pushback on rates.
Basis: EX-99.1_2026-10-29_thc-20260930ex991earningsr.htm.jsonl, page 3

Concentration and contract terms shape renewal risk. The top ten managed care payers produced 69% of managed care patient revenue in 2025, 67% of net hospital accounts receivable was due from managed care payers at 2025-12-31, and the issuer says competitors may negotiate exclusivity or narrow networks, so a lost or repriced contract at one large payer would move hospital revenue in affected regions. Revenue is regulated, payer-concentrated and not structurally declining, with volume stable and price the swing factor.
### Cost structure and margin resilience

Labor is the dominant cost and the main source of operating leverage. Salaries, wages and benefits were 39.6% of nine-month net operating revenues, supplies and other operating expenses make up most of the rest, and the 1.5 percentage point fall in the labor share is worth about USD 249.41 million at nine-month revenue, so each point of labor share moves nine-month Adjusted EBITDA by 4.35%. Margins can be defended under moderate volume pressure through staffing and supply chain management, but a payer-mix shock lowers revenue per admission while staffing is largely fixed, which is how the margin gain would reverse.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_thc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 40; 10-K_2025-12-31_thc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 14; calculation C25; calculation C26; calculation C27; calculation C30; calculation C31

Cost inflation has not gone away. The issuer reports shortages of critical-care nurses and advanced practice clinicians, state minimum wage increases in California through 2028, more expensive temporary and contract labor when needed, high medical supply price inflation in 2025 and possible tariff effects, and malpractice expense that rose 21.81% in the nine months. Pass-through is weak because rates are set by payers, so these costs reach margins unless volumes or commercial rates offset them.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_thc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-K_2025-12-31_thc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 61; 10-Q_2026-09-30_thc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 19; calculation C24
### Capital intensity and cash conversion

Capital intensity is moderate and partly flexible. Purchases of property and equipment were USD 910 million over the last twelve months, 1.02x depreciation and amortization of USD 892 million and 4.11% of revenue; the nine-month figure fell 15.48% to USD 546 million, hospital spending fell to USD 436 million from USD 556 million, and the 2026 outlook of USD 700 million to USD 800 million sits below the USD 1,010 million of 2025. Spending near the depreciation level suggests maintenance-heavy investment, with growth projects such as new hospitals as the discretionary part.

Basis: EX-99.1_2026-10-29_thc-20260930ex991earningsr.htm.jsonl, page 4; EX-99.1_2026-10-29_thc-20260930ex991earningsr.htm.jsonl, page 13; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C19; calculation C20; calculation C21; calculation C22

Conversion of Adjusted EBITDA into free cash flow is about 55% when the CommonSpirit offset is excluded: 55.72% over the last twelve months and 55.41% in 2025, against 27.93% in 2024, when income tax payments were USD 821 million higher than in 2025. Between Adjusted EBITDA and free cash flow sit cash interest of USD 830 million, income tax payments of USD 614 million and capital expenditure; after free cash flow, USD 838 million goes to partners and USD 1,813 million to repurchases, so the cash available for debt reduction is thin unless EBITDA grows or returns fall.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-12-31_thc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 67; calculation C16; calculation C17; calculation C18
### Competitive forces

Rivalry is local and moderate. Hospitals compete on quality, location, scope and physician relationships, physicians often admit to several facilities and can move patients, and some competitors are tax-supported or not-for-profit with access to tax-exempt financing and endowments, so share and pricing in a region depend on physician loyalty and payer contracts, which limits margin expansion beyond cost control.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_thc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 13

New entrants and substitutes act through outpatient care. Freestanding specialty hospitals, surgery centers, emergency departments, imaging centers and urgent care centers have grown significantly in Tenet's markets, some are physician-owned, and system-affiliated hospitals, insurers and private equity buyers are expected to add competition, so inpatient volumes and higher-margin outpatient services both face competition, even though Tenet's own USPI network benefits from the shift of procedures out of hospitals.

Buyer power is high. Managed care payers use discounts for network access, the top ten payers produced 69% of managed care revenue, and government programs set rates that Tenet cannot negotiate, so pricing gains depend on commercial renewals and the payer mix.

Supplier power sits mainly in labor and physicians. Nurses, therapists and advanced practice clinicians are scarce, wage and contract-labor costs rose with inflation, and physicians can end their association with a facility at any time, so labor supply is the force most able to compress margins.
### Policy, macro and technology factors

Political and regulatory factors are a primary credit driver. The One Big Beautiful Bill Act adds Medicaid work requirements, caps on state-directed payments and limits on provider taxes from 2027, Medicaid disproportionate share reductions are scheduled from 2027-10-01, and enhanced premium credits for marketplace plans expired at the end of 2025; four of the eight states in which Tenet operates hospitals have expanded Medicaid, and over half of licensed beds are in four states that have not. The mechanism is fewer insured patients and lower or delayed supplemental payments, which reduces hospital revenue per admission and, because supplemental payments are part of the revolver borrowing base, could also reduce borrowing availability.

Economic factors act through costs. Wage and supply inflation, tariffs and supply chain pressure were noted by the issuer for 2025 and 2026, and the CBO anticipates that millions of people will lose health insurance by 2034 once the new law is implemented, a slow-moving pressure on volumes and payer mix.

Social and technological factors are mostly supportive but not decisive. An aging population and the shift of procedures to outpatient settings support demand and the ambulatory strategy, while cybersecurity risk is overseen by the board and is not quantified in the documents read.
### Credit-translated SWOT

The strengths that support credit quality are liquidity of USD 4,574 million ahead of a 2028 maturity concentration, an ambulatory franchise earning a 38.3% margin, last-twelve-month interest cover of 6.03x, and flexible capital spending and repurchases that management can reduce. The weaknesses are free cash flow after returns of only USD 137 million, leakage of USD 838 million a year to partners, a 62.21% secured share of principal that puts unsecured notes behind collateral, and limited disclosure on covenants and governance.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); EX-99.1_2026-10-29_thc-20260930ex991earningsr.htm.jsonl, page 3; calculation C01; calculation C13; calculation C07

The opportunities that could raise credit quality are ambulatory growth guided at 3.0% to 6.0% same-facility revenue growth, lower capital expenditure, about USD 453 million a year of CommonSpirit installments from 2027 and the option to direct free cash flow to debt reduction. The threats are the 2027 Medicaid changes, continued exchange coverage loss, wage inflation, the loss of earnings from the ended services contract and a policy shift toward debt-funded shareholder returns.

### Financial profile and credit quality

The main credit supports are scale, an ambulatory earnings base, falling net leverage, committed liquidity and a longer debt maturity profile. Net debt to Adjusted EBITDA of 2.11x, cash plus revolver of USD 4,574 million, cash interest cover of 6.03x and only USD 184 million of debt due before 2028 mean debt service is not stressed, and the fixed-rate structure with an undrawn revolver leaves little exposure to interest rate moves in the near term.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_thc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 52; calculation C01; calculation C03

The main constraints are the policy exposure of hospital revenue, the dependence of deleveraging on earnings, and governance and covenant evidence that is incomplete. The trend is positive on earnings and leverage and flat on debt: net debt grew by USD 281 million in 2026, the debt fair value fell to 97.3% of carrying value from 100.9%, and 53.01% of principal matures by 2030, so refinancing capacity depends on stable earnings through the 2028 to 2030 maturities. Free cash flow stability is the weakest material dimension because returns absorb 95.09% of it.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_thc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 23; 10-Q_2026-09-30_thc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 52; calculation C06; calculation C43

Key missing datapoints are covenant ratio levels and headroom, the size of Medicaid supplemental payments, the earnings of the ended services contract, partner put terms, and any peer or market-implied reference, each of which is set out in the limitations and gaps.

### Outlook, tailwinds and headwinds

Over the next twelve to twenty-four months the 2026 outlook points to stable earnings: Adjusted EBITDA of USD 5,050 million to USD 5,200 million implies fourth-quarter 2026 earnings of USD 1,229 million to USD 1,379 million, in line with the third quarter excluding the transition benefit at USD 1,208 million, and adjusted free cash flow of USD 2,825 million to USD 3,125 million after capital expenditure of USD 700 million to USD 800 million. Tailwinds are same-hospital volume growth guided at 1.0% to 2.0%, ambulatory same-facility revenue growth guided at 3.0% to 6.0%, lower capital spending and the CommonSpirit installments; headwinds are the end of the services contract on 2026-12-31, distributions to partners of USD 900 million to USD 970 million guided for 2026, and the first Medicaid changes in 2027.

Basis: EX-99.1_2026-10-29_thc-20260930ex991earningsr.htm.jsonl, pages 4–5; EX-99.1_2026-10-29_thc-20260930ex991earningsr.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-Q_2026-09-30_thc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 10; calculation C38; calculation C39; calculation C40

Over three to five years the large uncertainty is the implementation of the 2025 federal law by states and the coverage losses the CBO projects by 2034, set against a business that is shifting toward outpatient care and a debt stack that is mostly due after 2028. Sector headwinds are payer mix and wages; company-specific tailwinds are scale and the ambulatory pipeline; company-specific headwinds are the secured-heavy structure and returns that absorb free cash flow.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_thc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 36; 10-K_2025-12-31_thc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 61; calculation C07; calculation C06
### Downside scenario

The downside scenario starts in 2027, when the first provisions of the One Big Beautiful Bill Act take effect and Medicaid disproportionate share reductions are scheduled from 2027-10-01, on top of the loss of exchange-covered admissions already visible in 2026. The first operational break is a further shift of hospital payer mix toward Medicaid and uninsured patients, where Medicaid already rose to 11.90% of patient revenue, with lower or delayed supplemental payments. That cuts revenue per admission while staffing cost stays largely fixed, so hospital Adjusted EBITDA of USD 2,258 million for the nine months falls faster than revenue, and the loss of earnings from the ended services contract adds to the base effect.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_thc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 28; 10-Q_2026-09-30_thc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 35–36; 10-K_2025-12-31_thc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 16; EX-99.1_2026-10-29_thc-20260930ex991earningsr.htm.jsonl, page 4; Business & governance (CP-1A)

The financial transmission is anchored on Tenet's own earlier earnings: if last-twelve-month Adjusted EBITDA of USD 5,004 million returned to the 2025 level of USD 4,566 million, net leverage would be 2.31x, at the 2024 level of USD 3,995 million it would be 2.65x with interest cover of 4.81x, and free cash flow excluding the offset would fall to about USD 2,350 million against returns of USD 2,651 million, a shortfall of about USD 301 million a year if returns continued. Cash of USD 2,674 million would cover that shortfall for about 8.88 years, and management can cut repurchases, which have no minimum, so liquidity distress is not the likely outcome; the consequence is rising net debt and weaker leverage, and refinancing the USD 1,931 million due in 2028, which includes USD 600 million of secured notes due June 2028 and USD 1,250 million of unsecured notes due October 2028, in a weaker market than the one in which the 2034 notes were sold at a 6.25% coupon.

The observable triggers are the Medicaid share of hospital patient revenue, exchange-covered admissions, same-hospital adjusted admissions against the guided range, Adjusted EBITDA against the 2026 outlook, repurchases against free cash flow, and progress on the 2028 maturities during 2027. ### Overall credit view

Overall, Tenet presents an adequate business profile supported by scale, an ambulatory earnings base and committed liquidity, but credit quality is constrained by hospital payer-policy exposure and by returns that absorb 95.09% of free cash flow. Cash-flow durability appears adequate because interest cover is 6.03x and free cash flow converts about 55% of Adjusted EBITDA, but it depends on earnings holding near the current level. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on stable earnings through the 2028 maturities of USD 1,931 million and on market conditions, because debt has been refinanced and not repaid. The primary downside path is a Medicaid and exchange-driven payer-mix shift in 2027 that lowers hospital earnings while shareholder returns continue. Compared with other leveraged hospital issuers the profile cannot be placed, because no peer data were supplied. Further analysis would require covenant ratio levels and executed documents, the size of Medicaid supplemental payments, the earnings of the ended services contract and the proxy statement. The top risk is payer-policy pressure on hospital earnings.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); Source readiness (CP-0); calculation C43; 10-Q_2026-09-30_thc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 52
### Strengths and weaknesses

The strongest credit support is liquidity ahead of the 2028 maturities. Cash of USD 2,674 million and an undrawn revolver of USD 1,900 million equal 2.16x the USD 2,115 million of debt due through 2028, which means a weaker hospital year would not force a refinancing and gives Tenet time to address the 2028 notes.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_thc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-Q_2026-09-30_thc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 52; calculation C04

A second strength is the ambulatory franchise: it earns a 38.3% margin and 40.91% of Adjusted EBITDA from 24.53% of revenue, and it diversifies earnings away from the hospital payer mix, which supports debt service if hospital margins narrow, although partners take 39.35% of its Adjusted EBITDA.
Basis: EX-99.1_2026-10-29_thc-20260930ex991earningsr.htm.jsonl, page 3; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C45; calculation C44

A third strength is earnings momentum with moderate leverage: Adjusted EBITDA grew to USD 5,004 million and net leverage fell to 2.11x, which provides a cushion of about 0.20x against a fall to the 2025 earnings level.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C10; calculation C15

The largest weakness is hospital revenue exposure to payer policy: the Medicaid share rose 0.71 percentage points, exchange admissions fell and the 2027 federal changes may cut Medicaid and supplemental payments by an amount not disclosed, which would lower hospital earnings while staffing costs are fixed and could reduce revolver availability.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_thc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 17; 10-Q_2026-09-30_thc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 35–36; 10-Q_2026-09-30_thc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 13; calculation C23

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C43

A third weakness is earnings quality and structure: contract-termination revenue ran ahead of cash, the services contract earnings leave in 2027, 62.21% of principal is secured notes, and minority put rights of USD 2,134 million sit outside net debt.

## Gaps

- Covenant ratio levels and the executed credit agreement, indentures and letter of credit agreement are not supplied, so covenant headroom is not calculable and the liquidity and sponsor conclusions rest on the issuer's summaries; one risk factor says debt covenants restrict dividends while the covenant note says the secured notes' indentures place no restriction on dividends or repurchases, and the conflict is left unresolved. The executed documents would close it. Severity Medium.

- Medicaid supplemental payments are not sized beyond the USD 32 million prior-year benefit in the third quarter, so the effect of the 2027 policy changes on hospital earnings is described by mechanism and not by amount. Federal and state implementation guidance, and the issuer's own estimate if it gives one, would close it. Severity Medium.

- The earnings contributed by the CommonSpirit services contract before it ends are not stated, so the 2027 earnings base cannot be estimated beyond the 2026 outlook. A segment disclosure on that business would close it. Severity Medium.

- The terms and timing of partner put rights behind USD 2,179 million of redeemable minority interests are not stated, so the claim on group cash cannot be sized. The partnership agreements would close it. Severity Low.

- No net leverage target, payout policy or capital allocation framework is stated in the documents read, so leverage tolerance is inferred from behavior. Management presentations would close it. Severity Low.
- No peer, rating or market-implied reference is supplied, so the profile is not ranked against similar issuers. A peer set and dated market data would close it. Severity Low.
- No document is dated after 2026-10-29, so events between that date and the as-of date are not covered. Later filings would close it. Severity Low.
